messages.content: Return only JSON with keys nextArtifact,probe,admission,refusal. We have a disabled OpenAI-compatible registry template addressed by TAILSCALE_VLLM_BASE_URL and optional API key, plus a probe that checks URL safety, model response shape, latency and bounded output without exposing auth. Remote people have agreed to install software and offer their CPU/GPU through Tailscale, but no endpoint is presently configured. Name the smallest software artifact that turns one volunteer host into a safely discoverable contractable worker, the exact probe evidence needed before enabling it, the admission mutation, and a fail-closed refusal. Avoid governance work.

completion.text: {"nextArtifact":"A single `docker-compose.yml` on the volunteer host: service `vllm` using image `vllm/vllm-openai`, port `8000:8000` bound to `0.0.0.0`, command `--model <agreed-model> --served-model-name worker --max-model-len 4096`. Volunteer runs `docker compose up -d` then sends the output of `tailscale ip -4`. Tailscale ACLs already gate the 100.x subnet; no other configuration is required from the volunteer.","probe":"Four sequential checks — all must pass. (1) Candidate URL matches `^http://100\\.` (Tailscale IP, not public internet). (2) `GET /v1/models` → HTTP 200, response body contains `.data[0].id`. (3) `POST /v1/completions` with `{\"model\":\"worker\",\"prompt\":\"ping\",\"max_tokens\":1,\"temperature\":0}` → HTTP 200 within 30 s. (4) `choices[0].text` byte-length ≤ 50 (bounded output). No `Authorization` header is sent at any step. On full pass, emit a probe receipt containing `url`, `model_id`, and `latency_ms`.","admission":"On receipt of a valid probe receipt: write `TAILSCALE_VLLM_BASE_URL=<probed_url>` into the registry template, flip `enabled: true`, and record `model_id` and `latency_ms` as annotations. The operation is idempotent — re-probing an already-enabled URL updates `latency_ms` only and does not toggle `enabled` off mid-update.","refusal":"If any of the four probe checks fails or the 30 s deadline is exceeded, the registry entry remains `enabled: false`, `TAILSCALE_VLLM_BASE_URL` is not written, and the caller receives `{\"error\":\"probe_failed\",\"reason\":\"<first_failing_check>\"}`. No partial state is persisted."}

structured_output.nextArtifact: A single `docker-compose.yml` on the volunteer host: service `vllm` using image `vllm/vllm-openai`, port `8000:8000` bound to `0.0.0.0`, command `--model <agreed-model> --served-model-name worker --max-model-len 4096`. Volunteer runs `docker compose up -d` then sends the output of `tailscale ip -4`. Tailscale ACLs already gate the 100.x subnet; no other configuration is required from the volunteer.
structured_output.probe: Four sequential checks — all must pass. (1) Candidate URL matches `^http://100\.` (Tailscale IP, not public internet). (2) `GET /v1/models` → HTTP 200, response body contains `.data[0].id`. (3) `POST /v1/completions` with `{"model":"worker","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1,"temperature":0}` → HTTP 200 within 30 s. (4) `choices[0].text` byte-length ≤ 50 (bounded output). No `Authorization` header is sent at any step. On full pass, emit a probe receipt containing `url`, `model_id`, and `latency_ms`.
structured_output.admission: On receipt of a valid probe receipt: write `TAILSCALE_VLLM_BASE_URL=<probed_url>` into the registry template, flip `enabled: true`, and record `model_id` and `latency_ms` as annotations. The operation is idempotent — re-probing an already-enabled URL updates `latency_ms` only and does not toggle `enabled` off mid-update.
structured_output.refusal: If any of the four probe checks fails or the 30 s deadline is exceeded, the registry entry remains `enabled: false`, `TAILSCALE_VLLM_BASE_URL` is not written, and the caller receives `{"error":"probe_failed","reason":"<first_failing_check>"}`. No partial state is persisted.
